name: Endpoint
summary: Host and endpoint forensic artifacts (files, processes, registry keys, services, mutexes, scheduled tasks) for DFIR and malware-behavior mapping.
description:
Node types for what an incident responder or malware analyst finds on a machine: the files, processes, registry entries, services, mutexes and persistence entries that show what ran on a host and how it stayed there.

The pack is data only: it defines six node types in the `endpoint` category and runs no code. It declares no edge types; how these nodes relate to each other is recorded as edges in the project.

## Types

| Type | Label | Identified by | What it represents |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `endpoint.file` | `file_name`, shown as `{file_name} · {hostname}` | `sha256`, `file_name`, `file_path`, `hostname` | A file observed on a host, with its hashes and path |
| `endpoint.process` | `process_name` | `process_guid`, `process_name`, `pid` | A running process observed on a host |
| `endpoint.registry_key` | `key_path` | `key_path`, `value_name` | A Windows registry key or value |
| `endpoint.service` | `service_name` | `service_name`, `binary_path` | A Windows service or system daemon |
| `endpoint.mutex` | `name` | `name` | A named synchronization object, commonly used by malware as an infection marker |
| `endpoint.persistence` | `name` | `name`, `mechanism` | A persistence mechanism: a scheduled task, an autostart Run key, a startup-folder entry, a WMI subscription, or similar |

"Identified by" is the set of properties that decides whether two nodes are the same entity.

## Notable properties

- **File.** `sha256`, `md5`, `size_bytes`, `mime_type`, `signed` and `file_path`. `hostname` is part of the identity: the same name and path on two machines is two files, and the type has no other way to tell them apart. It stays blank when the source does not say. `sha256` and `hostname` are matched without regard to case.
- **Process.** `process_guid` holds a stable per-execution id such as the Sysmon or EDR ProcessGuid. It is the reliable process identity, because image names and PIDs both recur. Also `pid`, `parent_pid`, `command_line`, `user` and `start_time`.
- **Registry key.** `hive` is one of `HKLM`, `HKCU`, `HKCR`, `HKU`, `HKCC`; `value_name` and `value_data` hold a value under the key.
- **Service.** `display_name`, `binary_path`, `start_type` (`auto`, `manual`, `disabled`, `boot`, `system`) and `state` (`running`, `stopped`, `paused`, and the four pending states).
- **Mutex.** `created_by` names the process or sample that created it, as text.
- **Persistence.** `mechanism` is one of `scheduled_task`, `run_key`, `service`, `startup_folder`, `wmi`, `other`; `trigger` says what starts it and `action` holds the command or action executed.

## Related types in other packs

- `threat.file_hash` in the Threat pack is a scanner's verdict on a sample, identified by its SHA-256 alone. `endpoint.file` is a file seen at a place on a host. The two are linked with an edge rather than merged.
- `threat.indicator` in the Threat pack is meant to be linked to the concrete node it identifies, such as an `endpoint.file`. Its `indicator_type` includes `filename`, `registry_key` and `mutex`.

## Source

https://github.com/Vineyard-Intelligence/typepack-basic (file `typepacks/endpoint.json`). Licence: Apache-2.0.

types.name: file
types.description: A file artifact observed on a host, with hashes and path. Identified by its content and where it was seen — two files with the same name on different machines are two nodes. For a scanner’s verdict on a sample, see threat.file_hash.

signed.description: Whether the file is digitally signed.

hostname.description: Host the file was observed on. Part of the identity: the same name and path on two machines is two files, and this type has no other way to tell them apart. Blank when the source does not say.

types.name: process
types.description: A running process observed on a host.

process_guid.description: Stable per-execution id (e.g. Sysmon/EDR ProcessGuid) — the reliable process identity, since image names and PIDs both recur.

types.name: registry_key
types.description: A Windows registry key or value.

types.name: service
types.description: A Windows service or system daemon.

types.name: mutex
types.description: A named synchronization object, commonly used by malware as an infection marker.

created_by.description: Process or sample that created the mutex.

types.name: persistence
types.description: A persistence mechanism — a scheduled task, autostart Run key, startup-folder entry, WMI subscription, or similar.
